examples.en: I take swimming lessons every weekend.
The class starts at seven in the evening.
Do you want to go to the yoga class together?
The instructor corrected my posture.
When this course ends, we take a test.
How much is the lesson fee per month?

explain: '수업'은 학교에서도 쓰지만 '강습'은 수영, 요가, 운전처럼 기술을 짧게 배우는 과정에 많이 써요. 배우는 것을 앞에 붙여 '수영 강습'이라고 하고, '강습을 받다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I signed up for a yoga lesson next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강습을 받다'보다 수업을 처음 등록하는 순간에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the moment of registering, whereas 'to take a lesson' is about attending.
phrases.en_equiv: to sign up for a lesson

phrases.en: The lesson is one hour long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강습이 진행되는 시간이나 길이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about when a lesson runs or how long it lasts.

phrases.en: How much is the swimming lesson fee?
phrases.nuance_ko: 강습에 내는 돈을 말해요. 학원비처럼 짧게 말할 때 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The money you pay for a course; a short, handy way to say the fee.

explain_en: 수업 is used at school too, but 강습 is mostly a short course for learning a skill such as swimming, yoga, or driving. Put the skill in front, as in '수영 강습', and say '강습을 받다' to take lessons.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 비가 적어 해마다 기우제를 지냈어요.
examples.en: That region gets little rain, so they held a rain ritual every year.
After a long drought, a rain ritual was held.

examples.ko: 이 마을에는 기우제에 얽힌 이야기가 전해져요.
examples.en: This village has a story about a rain ritual passed down.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 옛 기우제의 모습을 영상으로 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum, I watched a video of an old rain ritual.

examples.ko: 비가 안 오면 기우제까지 지낸다고 하더라고요.
examples.en: They say that if it doesn't rain, they even hold a rain ritual.

examples.ko: 그 마을은 기우제도 지내고 우물도 새로 팠어요.
examples.en: That village held a rain ritual and also dug a new well.

explain: 가뭄 때 비를 내려 달라고 빌던 제사예요. '기우제를 지내다'처럼 '지내다'와 같이 써요. 역사나 전통 이야기에서 자주 만나는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The villagers held a rain ceremony on the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지내다'보다 정성을 들여 바치는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels a bit more like making a sincere offering than '지내다'.

phrases.en: In the old days, there was a custom of holding rain ceremonies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전통이나 역사 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used in stories about tradition or history.
phrases.en_equiv: the custom of holding a rain ceremony

phrases.example: 가뭄과 기우제에 대한 이야기를 책에서 읽었어요.
phrases.en: I read a story about droughts and rain ceremonies in a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기우제는 가뭄과 함께 이야기하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rain ceremonies are often discussed together with droughts.

explain_en: It is the ritual people performed to pray for rain during a drought. It goes with '지내다', as in '기우제를 지내다'. You mostly meet it in stories about history and tradition.

examples.en: I toughen up my body by running every day.
He trained his mind from a young age.
Swimming is good for building up your body.
I signed up at the gym to build my stamina.

examples.ko: 선수들은 겨울 동안 더 열심히 단련할 거예요.
examples.en: The players will train even harder during the winter.

examples.ko: 매일 단련하면 어려운 동작도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you train every day, you can do difficult moves too.

explain: '운동하다'는 몸을 움직이는 일반적인 말이고, '단련하다'는 몸이나 마음을 반복해서 강하게 만든다는 느낌이 있어요. '몸을 단련하다', '정신을 단련하다'처럼 목적어는 주로 몸·마음·기술이에요.

phrases.en: My body was toughened through long training.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단련을 받아 강해진 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the thing that became strong through training is the subject.

phrases.en: I train my mind through meditation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸뿐 아니라 마음도 반복해서 강하게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not only the body, but the mind too, is strengthened through repetition.

phrases.example: 좋은 몸을 만들려면 꾸준한 단련이 필요해요.
phrases.en: To build a good body, steady training is needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단련'은 명사로도 쓰고, '꾸준한'과 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 단련 also works as a noun and often appears with 꾸준한.

explain_en: '운동하다' is the general word for exercising, while '단련하다' carries the sense of repeatedly making your body or mind stronger. Its objects are mostly body, mind, or skill, as in '몸을 단련하다' and '정신을 단련하다'.

examples.ko: 에베레스트 등정에 성공한 사람이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A person who succeeded in climbing Everest appeared on the news.

examples.ko: 그 등산가는 히말라야 등정을 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: That mountaineer is preparing for a Himalayan expedition.

examples.ko: 이번 겨울 한라산 등정은 눈 때문에 미뤄졌어요.
examples.en: This winter's Hallasan climb was postponed because of the snow.
The weather turned bad during the climb, so we turned back.

examples.ko: 여성 최초 등정 기록이 오래전에 세워졌어요.
examples.en: The record for the first woman to reach the summit was set long ago.
After the summit climb ended, everyone came down safely.

explain: 산, 특히 높은 산의 정상에 오르는 일을 말해요. 일상의 '등산'과 달리 정상을 목표로 한 도전과 기록의 느낌이 있어요. '등정에 성공하다', '등정을 마치다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 날씨가 나빴지만 등정에 성공했어요.
phrases.en: The team succeeded in reaching the summit despite the bad weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정상에 오른 도전을 알릴 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for announcing a successful summit climb.

phrases.example: 일행은 사흘 만에 등정을 마치고 내려왔어요.
phrases.en: The group finished the ascent in three days and came down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라갔다 오는 일이 끝났다는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Conveys that the climb is completed.

phrases.example: 그는 에베레스트 등정을 평생 꿈꿔 왔어요.
phrases.en: He has dreamed of climbing Everest all his life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산 이름 뒤에 붙여 특정 산의 정상 도전을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach it after a mountain's name to refer to a summit attempt.

explain_en: It means climbing a mountain, especially up to the summit of a high one. Unlike everyday '등산' (hiking), it carries a sense of a challenge and a record aimed at the peak. It is used as in '등정에 성공하다' and '등정을 마치다'.

examples.en: Ahead of the tournament, the players went into intense training.

examples.ko: 한 달 동안 맹훈련을 했더니 기록이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After a month of hard training, my record improved.

examples.ko: 맹훈련 덕분에 시험 준비가 잘 됐어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the intense practice, my exam preparation went well.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 매일 저녁 맹훈련 중이에요.
examples.en: Our club is in intense training every evening.
I built up my body with hard training all winter.

examples.ko: 이번 주는 맹훈련이 계속돼서 정말 피곤해요.
examples.en: The intense training keeps going this week, so I'm really tired.

explain: '맹훈련을 하다', '맹훈련에 들어가다', '맹훈련을 거듭하다'처럼 써요. 운동선수 뉴스에 자주 나오지만 시험이나 공연 준비를 힘들게 했다고 말할 때도 쓸 수 있어요. '맹연습', '맹활약'처럼 '맹-'은 기세가 거센 느낌을 더해요.

phrases.en: The players went into hard training ahead of the match.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본격적으로 힘든 훈련을 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting serious, tough training.

phrases.en: That team trained hard again and again to win the championship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘든 훈련을 여러 번 반복한다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of repeating tough training many times.

phrases.example: 공연 전에 맹연습을 해서 목이 아파요.
phrases.en: I practiced intensely before the performance, so my throat hurts.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹훈련'과 비슷하지만 노래나 공연, 악기처럼 연습에 더 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '맹훈련', but fits practice such as singing, performances, or instruments better.

explain_en: It is used as '맹훈련을 하다', '맹훈련에 들어가다' or '맹훈련을 거듭하다'. It often appears in sports news, but you can also use it for hard preparation for an exam or a performance. Like '맹연습' and '맹활약', the '맹-' prefix adds a fierce, intense feel.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌 무패 행진을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is continuing its unbeaten streak this season.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 데뷔 이후 무패로 은퇴했어요.
examples.en: That player retired undefeated since his debut.
Ten games unbeaten is really impressive.

examples.ko: 그 팀의 무패 기록이 드디어 깨졌어요.
examples.en: That team's unbeaten record has finally been broken.
We're training with the goal of winning the title unbeaten.
The team that boasted of being unbeaten lost for the first time.

explain: '지지 않았다'는 뜻이라 비긴 경기가 있어도 무패예요. 모두 이긴 '전승'과 달라요. 반대말은 '전패'예요. 스포츠에서 주로 써요.

phrases.en: That team won the title without a single loss.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번도 지지 않고 우승했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means winning the championship without losing once.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 열 경기 무패 기록을 세웠어요.
phrases.en: That player set a ten-game unbeaten record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지지 않은 경기 수를 기록으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a record of games without a loss.

phrases.en: Our team finished the season undefeated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무패로'를 붙이면 결과가 어떠했는지를 짧게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '무패로' briefly states how the outcome went.

explain_en: It means 'never lost', so a record with draws is still '무패'. That differs from '전승', which means winning every game. The opposite is '전패'. It is mainly used in sports.

examples.en: At the last moment, the coach played a decisive card.
The company bet everything on its new product.

examples.ko: 이번 면접에서 저는 경험을 승부수로 삼았어요.
examples.en: In this interview, I made my experience my key weapon.
That player's final gamble worked.

examples.ko: 지금은 가격을 낮추는 것이 최고의 승부수예요.
examples.en: Right now, lowering the price is the best decisive move.
Now is the time when you need a decisive move.

explain: 경기나 사업에서 승패를 가를 결정적인 한 수를 말해요. 거의 '승부수를 던지다'로 쓰고, 뉴스나 스포츠 기사에서 자주 보여요. '비장의 카드'와 비슷하지만 승부수는 위험을 감수하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: to stake everything on one decisive move
phrases.nuance_ko: 성공하면 크게 이기지만 실패하면 위험한 결정적인 선택을 할 때 써요. 뉴스, 스포츠, 사업 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone makes a bold, decisive choice that could win big but is risky if it fails. Common in news, sports and business stories.

explain_en: It means the one decisive move that decides win or loss in a game or in business. It is almost always used as '승부수를 던지다' and appears often in news and sports articles. It is close to '비장의 카드' (trump card), but 승부수 carries a stronger sense of taking a risk.

examples.en: I rode a hot-air balloon and looked down at the town from the sky.
At the travel destination, hot-air balloons rose one by one at dawn.

examples.ko: 열기구는 바람이 강한 날에는 못 떠요.
examples.en: Hot-air balloons can't fly on windy days.

examples.ko: 저는 높은 곳이 무서워서 열기구 타기가 겁나요.
examples.en: I am afraid of heights, so riding a hot-air balloon scares me.
We took a family photo inside the hot-air balloon.

examples.ko: 커다란 열기구는 뜨거운 공기로 천천히 올라가요.
examples.en: A huge hot-air balloon slowly rises on hot air.

explain: '열기구를 타다'처럼 '타다'와 같이 써요. 하늘을 나는 탈것으로 '비행기', '헬리콥터'도 있지만 열기구는 천천히 떠올라 풍경을 구경하는 관광 이미지가 강해요.

phrases.example: 아이들이 열기구를 타 보고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: The children want to try riding a hot-air balloon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열기구와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb most often used with 열기구.

phrases.en: I tried a hot-air balloon ride in Türkiye.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행이나 관광 활동을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about travel or tourist activities.

phrases.example: 가을에 열기구 축제가 열려서 구경하러 갔어요.
phrases.en: A hot-air balloon festival was held in autumn, so I went to watch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 열기구가 한꺼번에 뜨는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to an event where many balloons rise at once.

explain_en: Say '열기구를 타다' with the verb '타다'. Other flying vehicles are '비행기' and '헬리콥터', but a '열기구' rises slowly and is mostly associated with sightseeing.

examples.en: This time I completed the full marathon.
My goal is to run all the way to the end.
My legs hurt, but I finished without giving up.
Next year I want to complete the ten-kilometer run.
They give a medal to everyone who finishes.
Even in the rain, the runners finished the whole course.

explain: 달리기, 자전거, 경주 같은 길을 처음부터 끝까지 다 마쳤을 때 써요. 등수와 상관없이 포기하지 않고 끝까지 갔다는 뿌듯함이 들어 있어요. 책을 끝까지 읽는 건 '완독하다', 드라마를 몰아 보는 건 '정주행하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 연습하면 십 킬로미터를 완주할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you practice, you can finish the ten kilometers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝까지 갈 수 있다는 가능을 말해요. 목표를 이야기할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses that finishing is possible, often used when talking about goals.

phrases.en: I hurt my leg, so I couldn't finish the course.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중간에 멈추게 된 아쉬운 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the disappointing situation of having to stop partway.

phrases.en: It was hard, but I finally made it to the finish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 내다'가 붙어서 어려움을 이기고 해냈다는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the 'make it through' ending strengthens the sense of overcoming difficulty.

explain_en: Used when you finish a whole route in running, cycling, or a race, regardless of your rank. It carries pride in not giving up. For finishing a book use 완독하다, and for binge-watching a drama use 정주행하다.

examples.en: The exploration expedition team set out for the Himalayas.
The expedition team reached the summit in a week.
The leader led the expedition team across the desert.

examples.ko: 원정대의 짐이 너무 많아서 말이 지쳤어요.
examples.en: The expedition's baggage was so heavy that the horses got worn out.

examples.ko: 원정대 중 한 명이 다쳐서 계획이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: One member of the expedition was hurt, so the plan changed.

examples.ko: 원정대에 들어가려면 체력 시험을 통과해야 해요.
examples.en: To join the expedition team you have to pass a fitness test.

explain: 산, 극지, 사막처럼 멀고 힘든 곳으로 가는 팀에 쓰고, 게임이나 판타지에서도 모험 파티를 이렇게 불러요. 운동 경기에서 상대 팀 경기장에 가는 팀은 보통 '원정 팀'이라고 해요. '원정 경기', '원정 응원'도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: The expedition members set up tents at the foot of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원정대에 속한 한 사람 한 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for each individual member of an expedition team.

phrases.en: I put together an expedition team with friends and went to the desert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 멀리 떠날 사람들을 모아 팀을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means gathering people to form a team for a long trip.

phrases.en: The expedition leader gave the members the signal to set off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원정대를 이끄는 책임자를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the person who leads an expedition team.

explain_en: It is used for teams going to far, hard places like mountains, polar regions, and deserts, and in games and fantasy a group of adventurers is also called this. In sports, a team that travels to the opponent's stadium is usually called an 원정 팀. Also learn 원정 경기 and 원정 응원.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 대충 읽지 말고 정독이 필요한 책이에요.
examples.en: This novel is a book that needs careful reading, not skimming.

examples.ko: 속독보다 정독이 이해에 더 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Close reading helps understanding more than speed reading.

examples.ko: 선생님은 방학 숙제로 소설 정독을 권하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher recommended reading a novel closely as vacation homework.

examples.ko: 정독 습관을 들이니까 글이 잘 이해돼요.
examples.en: Since I built a habit of close reading, I understand texts better.
I prefer close reading to reading many books.

examples.ko: 정독 후에 느낀 점을 짧게 써 오세요.
examples.en: Please write briefly about what you felt after reading it closely.

explain: 한 줄씩 뜻을 새기며 꼼꼼하게 읽는 방법을 말해요. 반대되는 말은 빨리 읽는 '속독', 책을 많이 읽는 '다독'이에요. 공부나 독서 이야기에서 '정독하다'와 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I read this book slowly and carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정독을 동사로 바꾼 말이라서 읽은 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 정독, used when talking about the act of reading.

phrases.en: A contract needs to be read carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대충 읽으면 안 되는 글에 대해 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for texts that shouldn't be skimmed.

phrases.en: Intensive reading and speed reading are different ways to read.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼼꼼히 읽는 것과 빨리 읽는 것을 비교할 때 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together to compare careful reading with fast reading.

explain_en: It refers to reading carefully, thinking about the meaning line by line. Its counterparts are '속독' (speed reading) and '다독' (reading many books). It often appears in talk about studying and reading, together with '정독하다'.

examples.en: The catcher threw the ball as soon as he caught it.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 포수는 어깨가 아주 강해요.
examples.en: Our team's catcher has a very strong arm.
Sitting with a catcher's mask on felt stuffy.
My younger brother plays catcher in baseball.
The catcher and the pitcher exchanged signs.
As a kid, my dream was to be a catcher on a baseball team.

explain: 야구에서 투수와 짝을 이루는 자리예요. 둘을 합쳐 '배터리'라고 불러요. 총으로 사냥하는 사람을 뜻하는 같은 소리의 '포수'도 있지만, 요즘은 야구 쪽이 더 흔해요.

phrases.en: I took the catcher position on my school baseball team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 자리를 맡을 때 '맡다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 맡다 for taking a position in baseball.

phrases.en: The pitcher and catcher together are called the battery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 둘이 짝으로 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two often appear as a pair.

phrases.en: I bought a new catcher's mitt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포수가 공을 받을 때 끼는 장갑을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the glove the catcher wears to receive the ball.

explain_en: In baseball it is the position paired with the 투수 (pitcher), and the two together are called the 배터리. There is also a 포수 with the same sound meaning a person who hunts with a gun, but today the baseball meaning is more common.
